chapters.title: The Wood of the Vine
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 15

1The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"Son of man, how is the wood of the vine better than any other wood,
the vine branch that is among the trees of the forest?

3Is wood taken from it to make anything?
Do people take a peg from it to hang any vessel on?

4It is thrown into the fire for fuel;
the fire has consumed both its ends, and its middle is charred.
Is it good for anything?

5Even when it was whole, it could not be made into anything;
how much less, when the fire has consumed it and it is charred,
can it ever be made into anything!

6Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: As the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so I have given up the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

7I will set My face against them; they have come out of the fire, but the fire will consume them; and you will know that I am the LORD, when I set My face against them.

8I will make the land a desolation, because they have broken faith, declares the Lord GOD."

Notes

  • v2 "the wood of the vine" — the vine was the prophets' picture of Israel: the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel (Isaiah 5:7), and I had planted you a choice vine (Jeremiah 2:21). Ezekiel asks only about its wood. A vine is valued for its fruit; without fruit, its wood is good for nothing.

  • vv4–5 "the fire has consumed both its ends, and its middle is charred" — a stick burnt at both ends: Jerusalem after the first exile, the one Ezekiel dates his visions by (1:2). How much less: if it was useless whole, it is useless now.

  • v7 "they have come out of the fire, but the fire will consume them" — those left in Jerusalem after the first fire will not escape the next.

  • v8 "because they have broken faith" — ma'alu ma'al, the verb and its own noun, the law's word for a breach of trust against the LORD: the treachery they committed against Me (Leviticus 26:40). Chapter 14 used the same words of a land that sins against Me by breaking faith (14:13).

chapters.title: The Foundling Bride
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 16

1The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"Son of man, make known to Jerusalem her detestable things,

3and say: This is what the Lord GOD says to Jerusalem: Your origin and your birth are of the land of the Canaanites; your father was an Amorite, and your mother a Hittite.

4As for your birth, on the day you were born your navel cord was not cut, you were not washed with water to cleanse you, you were not rubbed with salt, and you were not wrapped in cloths.

5No eye pitied you, to do any one of these things for you out of compassion; you were thrown out into the open field, so loathed were you on the day you were born.

6I passed by you and saw you kicking about in your blood, and I said to you in your blood, 'Live!' I said to you in your blood, 'Live!'

7I made you grow like a plant of the field, and you grew up and became tall and came to full beauty; your breasts were formed and your hair had grown, yet you were naked and bare.

8I passed by you again and saw you, and your time was the time for love. I spread My wing over you and covered your nakedness; I swore an oath to you and entered into a covenant with you, declares the Lord GOD, and you became Mine.

9Then I washed you with water, rinsed your blood off you, and anointed you with oil.

10I clothed you with embroidered cloth and put sandals of fine leather on your feet; I wrapped you in fine linen and covered you with silk.

11I adorned you with ornaments, put bracelets on your arms and a chain around your neck,

12a ring in your nose, earrings in your ears, and a beautiful crown on your head.

13So you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothing was fine linen, silk and embroidered cloth. You ate fine flour, honey and oil; you became exceedingly beautiful and rose to be a queen.

14Your fame went out among the nations because of your beauty, for it was perfect through My splendor that I had put on you, declares the Lord GOD.

The Bride Who Prostituted Herself

15But you trusted in your beauty and prostituted yourself on the strength of your fame, and poured out your prostitution on everyone who passed by; it was his.

16You took some of your garments and made for yourself high places decked with many colors, and prostituted yourself on them; such things have never been and never shall be.

17You took your beautiful jewels, of My gold and My silver that I had given you, and made for yourself images of men, and prostituted yourself with them.

18You took your embroidered garments and covered them, and set My oil and My incense before them.

19My bread that I gave you, the fine flour, oil and honey with which I fed you, you set before them as a soothing aroma; so it was, declares the Lord GOD.

20You took your sons and your daughters whom you had borne to Me and sacrificed them to these images to be devoured. Was your prostitution so small a thing,

21that you slaughtered My children and gave them up to them, making them pass over to them?

22In all your detestable things and your prostitution you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, kicking about in your blood.

23After all your wickedness — woe, woe to you, declares the Lord GOD —

24you built yourself a mound and made yourself a lofty place in every square.

25At the head of every road you built your lofty place and made your beauty detestable, spreading your legs to everyone who passed by, and multiplied your prostitution.

26You prostituted yourself with the Egyptians, your neighbors, great of flesh, and multiplied your prostitution to provoke Me.

27So I stretched out My hand against you, cut down your portion, and gave you over to the will of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your lewd way.

28You prostituted yourself with the Assyrians, because you were never satisfied; you prostituted yourself with them, and still you were not satisfied.

29You multiplied your prostitution with the land of traders, Chaldea, and even with this you were not satisfied.

30How sick is your heart, declares the Lord GOD, that you did all these things, the deeds of a brazen prostitute,

31building your mound at the head of every road and making your lofty place in every square! Yet you were not like a prostitute, because you scorned payment.

32You adulterous wife, who takes strangers instead of her husband!

33All prostitutes are given gifts, but you gave your gifts to all your lovers, and bribed them to come to you from every side for your prostitution.

34So you were the opposite of other women in your prostitution: no one solicited you, and you gave payment when no payment was given to you. You were the opposite.

The Judgment

35Therefore, prostitute, hear the word of the LORD.

36This is what the Lord GOD says: Because your copper was poured out and your nakedness uncovered in your prostitution with your lovers and with all your detestable idols, and because of the blood of your children whom you gave to them,

37therefore I am about to gather all your lovers with whom you took pleasure, all whom you loved and all whom you hated; I will gather them against you from every side and uncover your nakedness to them, and they will see all your nakedness.

38I will judge you with the judgments of women who commit adultery and shed blood, and bring on you the blood of wrath and jealousy.

39I will give you into their hands, and they will tear down your mound and break down your lofty places; they will strip you of your clothes, take your beautiful jewels and leave you naked and bare.

40They will bring up an assembly against you, and they will stone you and cut you to pieces with their swords.

41They will burn your houses with fire and carry out judgments on you in the sight of many women. I will put an end to your prostitution, and you will no longer give payment.

42So I will satisfy My wrath on you, and My jealousy will turn away from you; I will be quiet and no longer angry.

43Because you did not remember the days of your youth but enraged Me with all these things, I in turn will bring your way on your own head, declares the Lord GOD. Have you not committed lewdness on top of all your detestable things?

Your Sisters

44Everyone who uses proverbs will use this proverb about you: 'Like mother, like daughter.'

45You are your mother's daughter, who loathed her husband and her children; and you are the sister of your sisters, who loathed their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.

46Your elder sister is Samaria, who lives with her daughters to the north of you; and your younger sister, who lives to the south of you, is Sodom with her daughters.

47You did not merely walk in their ways and do as their detestable things; as if that were too little, you were more corrupt than they in all your ways.

48As I live, declares the Lord GOD, your sister Sodom and her daughters have not done as you and your daughters have done.

49This was the iniquity of your sister Sodom: she and her daughters had pride, plenty of bread and careless ease, but did not strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.

50They were haughty and did detestable things before Me, so I removed them when I saw it.

51Samaria did not commit half your sins. You have multiplied your detestable things more than they, and by all the detestable things you have done you have made your sisters look righteous.

52You also must bear your disgrace, for you have pleaded for your sisters: because of your sins, in which you acted more detestably than they, they are more righteous than you. So be ashamed, you also, and bear your disgrace, for you have made your sisters look righteous.

53I will restore their fortunes, the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters and the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters, and your own fortunes along with them,

54so that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all you have done, when you become a comfort to them.

55Your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, will return to what they were before, and Samaria and her daughters will return to what they were before, and you and your daughters will return to what you were before.

56Was not your sister Sodom a byword in your mouth in the day of your pride,

57before your wickedness was uncovered? Now you are like her, the reproach of the daughters of Aram and of all around her, the daughters of the Philistines, who despise you on every side.

58You bear your lewdness and your detestable things, declares the LORD.

An Everlasting Covenant

59For this is what the Lord GOD says: I will deal with you as you have done, you who despised the oath by breaking the covenant.

60Yet I Myself will remember My covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with you.

61Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed, when you receive your sisters, those older and younger than you; and I will give them to you as daughters, but not by your covenant.

62I Myself will establish My covenant with you, and you will know that I am the LORD,

63so that you may remember and be ashamed, and never open your mouth again because of your disgrace, when I make atonement for you for all you have done, declares the Lord GOD."

Notes

  • v3 "your father was an Amorite, and your mother a Hittite" — Jerusalem was the city of the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, before David took it (2 Samuel 5:6–7), and the oracle gives her the parents of the land's old peoples. In v45 the same parents explain why the daughter is like them.

  • vv4–6 "your navel cord was not cut… you were thrown out into the open field… I said to you in your blood, 'Live!'" — a newborn left to die, without the care every child was given at birth. In your blood, 'Live!' is said twice in the Hebrew; the Greek has it once.

  • v8 "I spread My wing over you and covered your nakedness" — kenafi, "My wing," the corner of the garment: Ruth's words to Boaz, Spread your wing over your servant, for you are a redeemer (Ruth 3:9). It is the act of taking a wife, and I entered into a covenant with you… and you became Mine says it outright.

  • vv10–13 "sandals of fine leather… fine linen and silk… fine flour, honey and oil" — tachash, the leather of the tabernacle's covering (Exodus 25:5), and meshi, found only here and in v13, taken as a fine cloth. She is dressed in the sanctuary's own materials, fine leather and fine linen (Exodus 25:4–5), and fed fine flour and oil, the stuff of the grain offering (Leviticus 2:1); in vv18–19 she sets them before idols.

  • vv15–34 "prostituted yourself… your prostitution" — zanah and its noun, more than twenty times in the chapter. The figure is the one Jeremiah used, you have prostituted yourself with many lovers (Jeremiah 3:1): the covenant is a marriage, and worship of other gods is unfaithfulness in it. The lovers are named as nations: Egypt (v26), Assyria (v28), Chaldea (v29).

  • v26 "your neighbors, great of flesh" — gidlei basar, a coarse phrase the English keeps as blunt as the Hebrew.

  • vv31–34 "you scorned payment… you gave payment when no payment was given to you" — the turn of the charge: she is worse than a prostitute, who is at least paid. Bribed them, tishchadi, is the word Kings uses of Ahaz, who sent the temple's silver and gold to the king of Assyria as a bribe (2 Kings 16:8).

  • v36 "Because your copper was poured out" — nechushtekh, from nechoshet, copper or bronze. The Greek also reads your copper, perhaps the payment of vv33–34; the word may also be a crude term for the body, and the sense is not certain.

  • vv46–52 "Samaria… Sodom… they are more righteous than you" — Sodom's sin is named here not as Genesis 19 tells it but as pride, plenty of bread and careless ease, and failing the poor and needy. Jerusalem has done worse than both her sisters, and God's verdict is that they look righteous beside her.

  • vv60–63 "I Myself will remember My covenant… an everlasting covenant… when I make atonement for you" — the chapter ends not with the stoning of vv40–41 but with God remembering the days of your youth, which she forgot (vv22, 43). Kapper, "make atonement," is the word of the altar, and here God does it Himself.

chapters.title: Two Eagles and a Cedar
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 17

1The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"Son of man, put a riddle and speak a parable to the house of Israel,

3and say: This is what the Lord GOD says:
A great eagle with great wings and long pinions,
full of feathers of many colors,
came to Lebanon
and took the top of the cedar.

4He plucked off the topmost of its young shoots
and carried it to a land of trade;
he set it in a city of merchants.

5Then he took some of the seed of the land
and put it in a field for seed;
he set it like a willow
beside many waters.

6It sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height,
its branches turned toward him
and its roots under him;
so it became a vine,
and it put out branches and sent out shoots.

7There was another great eagle,
with great wings and many feathers;
and this vine bent its roots toward him
and sent out its branches toward him,
from the beds where it was planted,
for him to water it.

8It had been planted in a good field, beside many waters,
to put out branches and bear fruit
and become a noble vine.

9Say: This is what the Lord GOD says:
Will it thrive?
Will he not pull up its roots
and strip off its fruit, so that it withers,
all its fresh sprouting leaves withered?
It will take no strong arm or many people
to lift it up by its roots.

10It is planted; will it thrive?
Will it not wither completely when the east wind strikes it,
wither on the beds where it sprouted?"

11The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

12"Say now to the rebellious house: Do you not know what these things mean? Say: The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and took its king and its princes and brought them to himself in Babylon.

13He took one of the royal line and made a covenant with him, putting him under an oath; and he took away the leading men of the land,

14so that the kingdom would be brought low and not lift itself up, but keep his covenant and stand by it.

15But he rebelled against him by sending his envoys to Egypt to be given horses and a large army. Will he thrive? Will the one who does such things escape? Can he break a covenant and escape?

16As I live, declares the Lord GOD, in the place of the king who made him king, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke, there in Babylon, with him, he shall die.

17Pharaoh with his great army and large company will not help him in the war, when ramps are thrown up and siege walls built to cut off many lives.

18He despised the oath by breaking the covenant; he gave his hand, and yet did all these things. He will not escape.

19Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: As I live, My oath that he despised and My covenant that he broke, I will bring it on his own head.

20I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My snare; I will bring him to Babylon and enter into judgment with him there for the treachery he committed against Me.

21All the fugitives of all his troops will fall by the sword, and those who are left will be scattered to every wind; and you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.

22This is what the Lord GOD says:
I Myself will take from the top of the lofty cedar and set it out;
from the topmost of its young shoots I will pluck off a tender one,
and I Myself will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.

23On the high mountain of Israel I will plant it,
and it will put out branches and bear fruit
and become a noble cedar.
Under it will live every bird of every wing;
in the shade of its branches they will live.

24All the trees of the field will know
that I am the LORD.
I bring low the high tree,
I make high the low tree,
I dry up the green tree,
and I make the dry tree flourish.
I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it."

Notes

  • v2 "put a riddle and speak a parable" — chud chidah u-meshol mashal, each verb with its own noun: the riddle of vv3–10, and the meaning in vv12–21.

  • vv3–4, 12 "A great eagle… came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar… The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and took its king" — the eagle is Nebuchadnezzar, and the cedar's top is the king he carried off with the leading men of the land, as Kings tells it: He carried Jehoiachin into exile to Babylon (2 Kings 24:15). A land of trade, eretz kena'an, is Babylon, as at 16:29.

  • vv5–6, 13–14 "some of the seed of the land… a spreading vine, low in height… He took one of the royal line and made a covenant with him" — Zedekiah, set on the throne under oath, a vine meant to stay low and turned toward the eagle. Like a willow, tsaftsafah, is found only here.

  • vv7, 15 "another great eagle… sending his envoys to Egypt to be given horses" — Pharaoh. The vine turns its roots toward the second eagle, and the king breaks his oath to seek Egypt's help.

  • vv16, 19–20 "in the place of the king who made him king… there in Babylon… he shall die… My oath that he despised" — Chronicles says Zedekiah rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God (2 Chronicles 36:13); the oath was sworn in God's name, so God calls it My oath and My covenant. What happened is in Jeremiah: the king of Babylon put out the eyes of Zedekiah… and put him in the house of custody until the day of his death (Jeremiah 52:11).

  • vv22–23 "I Myself will take from the top of the lofty cedar… On the high mountain of Israel I will plant it" — the riddle turned: what the eagle did, God now does, I Myself, and the shoot He plants becomes a cedar where every bird of every wing lives.

  • v24 "I bring low the high tree, I make high the low tree" — the song of Hannah has the same reversal in other words (1 Samuel 2:7–8): what is high and green is not safe, and what is low and dry is not lost.

chapters.title: The Soul Who Sins Shall Die
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 18

1The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"What do you mean by using this proverb about the land of Israel, saying,
'The fathers eat sour grapes,
and the children's teeth are set on edge'?

3As I live, declares the Lord GOD, you shall no longer use this proverb in Israel.

4All souls are Mine: the soul of the father as well as the soul of the son is Mine. The soul who sins shall die.

5If a man is righteous and does what is just and right,

6if he does not eat on the mountains or lift his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, does not defile his neighbor's wife or come near a woman in her impurity,

7does not oppress anyone, but gives back the debtor his pledge, commits no robbery, gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing,

8does not lend at interest or take any increase, keeps his hand from wrong, does true justice between man and man,

9walks in My statutes and keeps My judgments by acting faithfully — he is righteous; he shall surely live, declares the Lord GOD.

10But if he fathers a son who is violent, who sheds blood and does any of these things

11(though the father did none of them), who eats on the mountains and defiles his neighbor's wife,

12oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, does not give back the pledge, lifts his eyes to the idols, does what is detestable,

13lends at interest and takes increase, shall he live? He shall not live. He has done all these detestable things; he shall surely be put to death. His blood will be on his own head.

14But if this man fathers a son who sees all the sins his father has done, and sees, and does not do the like,

15who does not eat on the mountains or lift his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, does not defile his neighbor's wife,

16does not oppress anyone, does not keep a pledge, commits no robbery, gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing,

17keeps his hand from the poor, takes no interest or increase, does My judgments and walks in My statutes, he shall not die for his father's iniquity; he shall surely live.

18As for his father, because he practiced extortion, robbed his brother, and did what is not good among his people, he has died for his iniquity.

19Yet you say, 'Why should the son not carry the guilt of the father?' When the son has done what is just and right, and has kept all My statutes and done them, he shall surely live.

20The soul who sins shall die. The son shall not carry the guilt of the father, nor the father carry the guilt of the son. The righteousness of the righteous will be on him, and the wickedness of the wicked will be on him.

21But if the wicked man turns from all the sins he has committed and keeps all My statutes and does what is just and right, he shall surely live; he shall not die.

22None of the transgressions he has committed will be remembered against him; for the righteousness he has done, he shall live.

23Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked, declares the Lord GOD, and not rather that he should turn from his ways and live?

24But when a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does wrong, doing all the detestable things the wicked man does, shall he live? None of the righteous deeds he has done will be remembered; for the treachery he has committed and the sin he has sinned, for them he shall die.

25Yet you say, 'The way of the Lord is not fair.' Hear now, house of Israel: Is My way not fair? Is it not your ways that are not fair?

26When a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does wrong, and dies for it, he dies for the wrong he has done.

27When a wicked man turns from the wickedness he has done and does what is just and right, he will save his life.

28Because he considered and turned from all the transgressions he had committed, he shall surely live; he shall not die.

29Yet the house of Israel says, 'The way of the Lord is not fair.' Are My ways not fair, house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are not fair?

30Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, each according to his ways, declares the Lord GOD. Turn, and turn away from all your transgressions, so that iniquity will not be your stumbling block.

31Throw away from you all the transgressions you have committed, and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why will you die, house of Israel?

32For I take no pleasure in the death of anyone who dies, declares the Lord GOD. So turn, and live."

Notes

  • vv2–4 "The fathers eat sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge" — the proverb Jeremiah too said would end: In those days they will no longer say, "The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge" (Jeremiah 31:29). Jeremiah put its end in the days to come; Ezekiel forbids it now.

  • vv4, 20 "The soul who sins shall die" — nefesh, the living person, the word of the life of the flesh is in the blood (Leviticus 17:11). The law said it of the courts: Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, and sons shall not be put to death for fathers (Deuteronomy 24:16). Ezekiel says it of God's judgment.

  • vv5–9 "if he does not eat on the mountains… does not lend at interest or take any increase" — the righteous man's life is measured by the law's own list: no worship at the high places, no adultery, no approach to a woman in the uncleanness of her monthly separation (Leviticus 18:19), the pledge returned (Exodus 22:26), no interest… and no increase (Leviticus 25:36).

  • vv9, 17, 19, 21, 28 "he shall surely live" — chayoh yichyeh, the doubled verb, answering the you shall surely die of the watchman's charge (3:18). The law's promise stands behind it: the person who does them shall live by them (Leviticus 18:5).

  • v13 "His blood will be on his own head" — the law's sentence on the one who curses his parents, his blood is on his own head (Leviticus 20:9); here the son's death is his own doing, not his father's.

  • vv23, 32 "Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked… So turn, and live" — the chapter turns from law to plea. The three generations show that no one is bound by his father's guilt, and the last verses say why God makes the case at all.

  • v31 "make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit" — in 11:19 God says I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; here the people are told to make one. The book holds both.

speech.text: Ezekiel 18
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
"What do you mean by using this proverb about the land of Israel, saying, 'The fathers eat sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge'?
As I live, declares the Lord GOD, you shall no longer use this proverb in Israel.
All souls are Mine: the soul of the father as well as the soul of the son is Mine. The soul who sins shall die.
If a man is righteous and does what is just and right,
if he does not eat on the mountains or lift his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, does not defile his neighbor's wife or come near a woman in her impurity,
does not oppress anyone, but gives back the debtor his pledge, commits no robbery, gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing,
does not lend at interest or take any increase, keeps his hand from wrong, does true justice between man and man,
walks in My statutes and keeps My judgments by acting faithfully — he is righteous; he shall surely live, declares the Lord GOD.
But if he fathers a son who is violent, who sheds blood and does any of these things
(though the father did none of them), who eats on the mountains and defiles his neighbor's wife,
oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, does not give back the pledge, lifts his eyes to the idols, does what is detestable,
lends at interest and takes increase, shall he live? He shall not live. He has done all these detestable things; he shall surely be put to death. His blood will be on his own head.
But if this man fathers a son who sees all the sins his father has done, and sees, and does not do the like,
who does not eat on the mountains or lift his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, does not defile his neighbor's wife,
does not oppress anyone, does not keep a pledge, commits no robbery, gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing,
keeps his hand from the poor, takes no interest or increase, does My judgments and walks in My statutes, he shall not die for his father's iniquity; he shall surely live.
As for his father, because he practiced extortion, robbed his brother, and did what is not good among his people, he has died for his iniquity.
Yet you say, 'Why should the son not carry the guilt of the father?' When the son has done what is just and right, and has kept all My statutes and done them, he shall surely live.

The soul who sins shall die. The son shall not carry the guilt of the father, nor the father carry the guilt of the son. The righteousness of the righteous will be on him, and the wickedness of the wicked will be on him.
But if the wicked man turns from all the sins he has committed and keeps all My statutes and does what is just and right, he shall surely live; he shall not die.
None of the transgressions he has committed will be remembered against him; for the righteousness he has done, he shall live.
Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked, declares the Lord GOD, and not rather that he should turn from his ways and live?

But when a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does wrong, doing all the detestable things the wicked man does, shall he live? None of the righteous deeds he has done will be remembered; for the treachery he has committed and the sin he has sinned, for them he shall die.
Yet you say, 'The way of the Lord is not fair.' Hear now, house of Israel: Is My way not fair? Is it not your ways that are not fair?

When a wicked man turns from the wickedness he has done and does what is just and right, he will save his life.

Yet the house of Israel says, 'The way of the Lord is not fair.' Are My ways not fair, house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are not fair?
Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, each according to his ways, declares the Lord GOD. Turn, and turn away from all your transgressions, so that iniquity will not be your stumbling block.
Throw away from you all the transgressions you have committed, and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why will you die, house of Israel?
For I take no pleasure in the death of anyone who dies, declares the Lord GOD. So turn, and live."

chapters.title: A Lament for the Princes of Israel
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 19

1"As for you, take up a lament for the princes of Israel,

2and say:
What a lioness was your mother
among the lions!
She lay down among young lions;
she reared her cubs.

3She brought up one of her cubs;
he became a young lion.
He learned to tear prey;
he devoured men.

4The nations heard about him;
he was caught in their pit,
and they brought him with hooks
to the land of Egypt.

5When she saw that she had waited in vain,
that her hope was lost,
she took another of her cubs
and made him a young lion.

6He prowled among the lions;
he became a young lion.
He learned to tear prey;
he devoured men.

7He knew their widows
and laid waste their cities;
the land and all in it were appalled
at the sound of his roaring.

8The nations set against him
from the provinces all around;
they spread their net over him;
he was caught in their pit.

9With hooks they put him in a cage
and brought him to the king of Babylon;
they brought him in nets,
so that his voice would no longer be heard
on the mountains of Israel.

10Your mother was like a vine in your blood,
planted by the waters;
she was fruitful and full of branches
because of many waters.

11She had strong stems
fit for the staffs of rulers.
Its height towered
among the thick branches,
and it was seen in its height
with the mass of its boughs.

12But it was torn up in fury
and thrown to the ground;
the east wind dried up its fruit;
its strong stems were broken off and withered;
the fire consumed it.

13Now it is planted in the wilderness,
in a dry and thirsty land.

14Fire has gone out from its stem
and consumed its shoots and its fruit,
so that there is no strong stem in it,
no staff to rule.
This is a lament, and it has become a lament."

Notes

  • v1 "take up a lament" — qinah, the song sung over the dead, here sung over the royal house of Judah. The chapter ends by naming itself the same way: This is a lament, and it has become a lament.

  • vv2–3 "What a lioness was your mother… one of her cubs… a young lion" — Jacob's blessing gave Judah the lion: A lion's cub is Judah… He crouched, he lay down like a lion, and like a lioness (Genesis 49:9). The mother is the royal house of Judah, and the cubs her kings.

  • vv3–4 "he was caught in their pit, and they brought him with hooks to the land of Egypt" — the cubs are not named. The first matches Jehoahaz, whom Pharaoh took away, and he came to Egypt and died there (2 Kings 23:34); the second, taken to the king of Babylon (v9), one of the kings carried there after him.

  • v7 "He knew their widows" — the Hebrew as it stands, va-yeda almenotav, "he knew his widows"; the sense is not certain. The Greek reads differently, he fed on his boldness. Read with v3's he devoured men, the widows are those he made.

  • v10 "Your mother was like a vine in your blood" — be-damkha, "in your blood," a phrase whose sense here is not settled; the same letters can also be heard as "in your likeness," from damah, "be like."

  • vv11, 14 "fit for the staffs of rulers… no staff to rule" — shevet, the word of Jacob's promise, The staff shall not turn aside from Judah (Genesis 49:10). The lament ends with the staff gone: the promise to Judah sung as a funeral song.

chapters.title: For the Sake of My Name
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 20

1And it came to pass in the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, that some of the elders of Israel came to inquire of the LORD, and sat before me.

2The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

3"Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and say to them: This is what the Lord GOD says: Have you come to inquire of Me? As I live, I will not let Myself be consulted by you, declares the Lord GOD.

4Will you judge them, will you judge them, son of man? Make known to them the detestable things of their fathers,

5and say to them: This is what the Lord GOD says: On the day I chose Israel, I raised My hand to the descendants of the house of Jacob and made Myself known to them in the land of Egypt; I raised My hand to them, saying, 'I am the LORD your God.'

6On that day I raised My hand to them to bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land I had searched out for them, flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands.

7I said to them, 'Each of you, throw away the loathsome things your eyes delight in, and do not make yourselves unclean with the idols of Egypt; I am the LORD your God.'

8But they rebelled against Me and would not listen to Me. They did not each throw away the loathsome things their eyes delighted in, nor did they forsake the idols of Egypt. So I said I would pour out My wrath on them and spend My anger on them in the middle of the land of Egypt.

9But I acted for the sake of My name, so that it would not be profaned in the sight of the nations among whom they were, in whose sight I had made Myself known to them by bringing them out of the land of Egypt.

10So I brought them out of the land of Egypt and led them into the wilderness.

11I gave them My statutes and made known to them My judgments, by which the person who does them shall live.

12I also gave them My sabbaths, to be a sign between Me and them, so that they would know that I am the LORD who sets them apart.

13But the house of Israel rebelled against Me in the wilderness. They did not walk in My statutes, and they rejected My judgments, by which the person who does them shall live, and they greatly profaned My sabbaths. So I said I would pour out My wrath on them in the wilderness to make an end of them.

14But I acted for the sake of My name, so that it would not be profaned in the sight of the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.

15I in turn raised My hand to them in the wilderness that I would not bring them into the land I had given them, flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands,

16because they rejected My judgments and did not walk in My statutes, and profaned My sabbaths, for their heart went after their idols.

17Yet My eye spared them from destruction, and I did not make an end of them in the wilderness.

18I said to their children in the wilderness, 'Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers or keep their judgments, or make yourselves unclean with their idols.

19I am the LORD your God. Walk in My statutes, keep My judgments and do them,

20and keep My sabbaths holy, so that they will be a sign between Me and you, that you may know that I am the LORD your God.'

21But the children rebelled against Me. They did not walk in My statutes or keep My judgments by doing them, by which the person who does them shall live; they profaned My sabbaths. So I said I would pour out My wrath on them and spend My anger on them in the wilderness.

22But I held back My hand and acted for the sake of My name, so that it would not be profaned in the sight of the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.

23I in turn raised My hand to them in the wilderness that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them through the countries,

24because they had not done My judgments but had rejected My statutes and profaned My sabbaths, and their eyes were set on their fathers' idols.

25I in turn gave them statutes that were not good, and judgments by which they could not live,

26and I made them unclean through their gifts, when they made every opener of the womb pass through the fire, so that I might devastate them, so that they would know that I am the LORD.

27Therefore speak to the house of Israel, son of man, and say to them: This is what the Lord GOD says: In this also your fathers blasphemed Me, by breaking faith with Me.

28When I had brought them into the land that I had raised My hand to give them, then wherever they saw any high hill or any leafy tree, there they offered their sacrifices, there they presented the offerings that provoked Me, there they set out their soothing aromas, and there they poured out their drink offerings.

29I said to them, 'What is this high place that you go to?' So its name is called High Place to this day.

30Therefore say to the house of Israel: This is what the Lord GOD says: Will you make yourselves unclean in the way of your fathers, and prostitute yourselves after their loathsome things?

31When you offer your gifts and make your sons pass through the fire, you make yourselves unclean with all your idols to this day. Shall I then let Myself be consulted by you, house of Israel? As I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will not let Myself be consulted by you.

32What comes into your mind will never happen, when you say, 'Let us be like the nations, like the clans of the countries, serving wood and stone.'

33As I live, declares the Lord GOD, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and with wrath poured out I will be king over you.

34I will bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the countries where you are scattered, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and with wrath poured out.

35I will bring you into the wilderness of the peoples, and there I will enter into judgment with you face to face.

36As I entered into judgment with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so I will enter into judgment with you, declares the Lord GOD.

37I will make you pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant.

38I will purge out from among you the rebels and those who transgress against Me; I will bring them out of the land where they live as guests, but they will not enter the land of Israel; and you will know that I am the LORD.

39As for you, house of Israel, this is what the Lord GOD says: Go, each of you serve his idols, now and afterward, if you will not listen to Me; but you shall no longer profane My holy name with your gifts and your idols.

40For on My holy mountain, the high mountain of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, there all the house of Israel, all of them in the land, will serve Me. There I will accept them, and there I will require your contributions and the first of your gifts, with all your holy things.

41As a soothing aroma I will accept you, when I bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the countries where you have been scattered; and I will show Myself holy among you in the sight of the nations.

42You will know that I am the LORD, when I bring you into the land of Israel, into the land I raised My hand to give to your fathers.

43There you will remember your ways and all the deeds by which you made yourselves unclean, and you will loathe yourselves for all the evils you have done.

44You will know that I am the LORD, when I deal with you for the sake of My name, not according to your evil ways or your corrupt deeds, house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD."

Fire in the Forest of the South

45The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

46"Son of man, set your face toward the south, preach against the south, and prophesy against the forest of the field in the Negev.

47Say to the forest of the Negev: Hear the word of the LORD! This is what the Lord GOD says: I am about to kindle a fire in you, and it will consume every green tree in you and every dry tree. The blazing flame will not be quenched, and every face from the Negev to the north will be scorched by it.

48All flesh will see that I, the LORD, have kindled it; it will not be quenched."

49Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! They are saying of me, 'Is he not just a maker of parables?'"

Notes

  • vv45–49 "set your face toward the south… the forest of the Negev" — the Hebrew prints these five verses as the opening of chapter 21 (21:1–5). English Bibles end chapter 20 with them, as Swete's Greek also does, and the numbers here follow the English.

  • vv1, 3, 31 "some of the elders of Israel came to inquire of the LORD… I will not let Myself be consulted by you" — a year after the vision of chapter 8 (the sixth year), the elders come again, and God refuses to be inquired of. What they get instead is the history of their fathers.

  • vv5–6, 15, 23, 28, 42 "I raised My hand" — nasa yad, the gesture of an oath, as at the exodus: I will bring you to the land that I raised My hand to give to Abraham (Exodus 6:8). The chapter turns on it: God raised His hand to bring them out (vv5–6), to keep them out of the land (v15), to scatter them (v23), and finally to bring them in (v42).

  • vv9, 14, 22, 44 "But I acted for the sake of My name" — four times the people rebel and God says He will pour out His wrath, and three times He holds back, not for their sake but so that His name would not be profaned in the sight of the nations. The last time (v44) He says it of the return.

  • vv11, 13, 21 "by which the person who does them shall live" — the law's own words, the person who does them shall live by them (Leviticus 18:5), set against v25.

  • vv12, 20 "My sabbaths, to be a sign between Me and them, so that they would know that I am the LORD who sets them apart" — Exodus 31:13 in the same words: it is a sign between Me and you… so that you may know that I am the LORD who sets you apart.

  • vv25–26 "I in turn gave them statutes that were not good… when they made every opener of the womb pass through the fire" — the hardest sentence in the chapter, and the verse does not explain it. The law said set apart to the LORD every opener of the womb (Exodus 13:12) and Every firstborn of man among your sons you shall redeem (13:13). Here the fathers make every opener of the womb pass through the fire, and God says He gave them statutes that were not good and made them unclean through their gifts: their own worship became the judgment on them.

  • v29 "'What is this high place that you go to?' So its name is called High Place" — a play on sounds: mah ha-bamah asher attem ha-ba'im sham, bamah "high place" and ba'im "you go."

  • vv33–38 "I will be king over you… I will make you pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant" — the second exodus will have its own wilderness, the wilderness of the peoples, and its own judgment. Passing under the rod is the counting of the flock, as in the law of the tithe, every tenth one that passes under the rod (Leviticus 27:32); the Greek reads I will bring you in by number.
